evidence.claim: Edison Research at SSRS, The Infinite Dial 2026: 'podcast and online audio consumption have reached all-time highs'; 84% of Americans 12+ use YouTube monthly (survey of 2,050 people, January 2026).
YouTube CEO letter lists podcasts among the formats viewers choose YouTube for, on 'every format on every screen'.

do: Write a guest brief (who they are, what they have done, five questions that lead to stories) and pick the cold-open line from the best moment of the conversation.

Title for YouTube search and curiosity: the guest or topic plus the specific promise ('Ex-food-delivery PM on why Tier-2 delivery fails'), with thumbnail text of 3-5 words that adds to the title, not repeats it (illustrative example).
Mark 3-5 clip moments with a one-line hook each, plus start and end timestamps.
Produce chapter markers and show notes with a two-line summary and three quotable lines.
dont: Do not reuse the audio title for the YouTube version.
Do not repeat the same hook across all clips.
Do not make claims about podcast listening shares without a source.
Do not write show notes that are transcripts dumped into the description.

cards.name: WhatsApp as acquisition and AI-agent sales channel
cards.summary: An ET report on GoKwik data says about 83% of orders generated through WhatsApp during the October-December festive quarter came from first-time buyers, and brands using its WhatsApp tools saw median GMV growth 2.25 times higher (vendor data); Meta said on its Q2 2026 call that Meta Business Agents are available globally on WhatsApp and Messenger, with more than 1 million businesses using them weekly to talk to customers or complete sales. Conversational copy, flows and agent personas are a paid deliverable for Indian D2C.
use_for: WhatsApp broadcast and template message copy
Bot flows, agent personas, FAQs and escalation lines
Order, cart and post-purchase message journeys
avoid: Long marketing paragraphs in a chat: each message gets one idea and one action.
Messaging without permission; follow opt-in and template-category rules (see plat:whatsapp_business_template), and use the template limits listed there.
Bot scripts with no human escalation line; customers need a way out.
Quoting GoKwik's figures as industry facts; they are one vendor's data.

sources.title: Economic Times: D2C brands turn to WhatsApp to win new customers
Meta Q2 2026 earnings call transcript

evidence.claim: ET on a GoKwik report: 'About 83% of orders generated through WhatsApp during the October-December festive quarter came from first-time buyers'; brands using its WhatsApp tools saw median GMV growth '2.25 times higher'.
Meta Q2 2026: Business Agents are live globally on WhatsApp and Messenger, and 'there are already more than 1 million businesses using them to talk to their customers or complete sales every week'

do: Write each broadcast as a short message with one idea, one offer detail and one button or reply ('Reply 1 to see sizes'), in the language the customer used to opt in.
Script the agent persona: name, tone, what it can do, what it will not do, and a clear handoff line ('Main aapko team se jod deta hoon').
Draft the FAQ answers as 1-2 sentence replies and the escalation triggers (refund, complaint, high-value order).
Map the journey: opt-in confirmation, order confirmation, shipping update, review request; keep each message transactional and useful.
Check opt-in wording and template categories with the client's ops before sending anything.
dont: Do not send promotions to people who did not opt in.
Do not use fake urgency or misleading offers.
Do not leave the bot without an exit to a human.
Do not write the same template for every customer segment.

cards.name: YouTube long-form watched on the TV screen
cards.summary: YouTube says over half of its top 100 creators have TV as their most-watched interface (Sep 2026), and its CEO's 2026 letter says 'YouTube is the new TV because creators are the new prime time.' The evidence is YouTube's own statement about top creators, not all viewers and not India, but the direction is clear: long-form can be watched lean-back on a TV, which rewards produced, structured scripts.
use_for: YouTube long-form scripts with a cold open, chaptered acts and a payoff
Titles, chapters and descriptions that work for a viewer scanning on a TV
Recaps and on-screen cues for viewers joining mid-video
avoid: Phone-only tricks like 'tap the link below' as the sole call to action: a TV viewer cannot tap. Put the action in words (the search phrase, the channel name, the next video).
Visuals that need a phone screen to read; keep on-screen text large and short so it reads across a room.
Dragging a 12-minute video on a 30-second idea; TV viewers tolerate length when the structure is clear.
Treating the top-100 statement as a general viewership stat.

sources.title: YouTube Official Blog, Made on YouTube 2026
sources.supports: TV as most-watched interface for top creators

sources.title: YouTube CEO letter 2026

evidence.claim: YouTube: 'Over half of YouTube's top 100 creators have TV as their most watched interface'.
YouTube CEO letter: 'YouTube is the new TV because creators are the new prime time.'

do: Write like television: a cold open that states the stakes in the first 30 seconds, then acts with chapter titles, and a payoff that matches the title's promise.
Add a one-line recap at the start of each major chapter for viewers who joined late or resumed.
Give calls to action in speakable form: 'Search our channel name and watch the next part' rather than 'link in the description'.
Write on-screen text in short large lines (a few words), and describe what the visual shows so the editor can plan wide, readable frames.
dont: Do not rely on tapping, scanning or clicking to complete the action.
Do not use tiny text and dense charts.
Do not open with a long intro before the stakes.
Do not leave chapters unnamed; they help both scanning and structure.
